summary: This article explains how tennis players use powerful serves and different kinds of spin, and how the court surface changes the way the ball bounces.
introduce: Write “Alike” and “Different” at the top of a T-chart on the board and ask students to compare two school subjects in one minute. Explain that “Tennis: Speed and Spin” asks them to make the same kind of comparison.

keyTerms.def: the person or team you play against
spin that makes the top of a ball turn forward, so the ball dips down

challengeTerms.def: the force that resists when one surface rubs or slides against another
the act of turning around a center point
the force of something pressing on an area

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that in tennis, spin is more important than speed? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain the difference between topspin and backspin, and tell why a player might choose each one.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review opponent, felt, and topspin, and let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use friction, rotation, and pressure in a short paragraph that compares two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
